title: TradingView Basics
hook: Your chart is your workspace. Learn it before you try to read it.

launchpad.outcome: Set up a clean, readable chart instead of a cluttered one.
launchpad.missionQuestion: Does adding more drawing tools to a chart make it easier to read, or harder?

slides.headline: Your chart is a workspace.
slides.line: Not a decoration contest. You’re here to read price, change perspective, and mark behavior.

cards.label: Read
cards.sub: Your chart’s job is showing you what price is doing.

cards.label: Zoom
cards.sub: Timeframes change your perspective, not the market.

cards.label: Mark
cards.sub: A few clean levels beat ten drawing tools.

cards.label: Simplify
cards.sub: If it doesn’t help you read price, take it off.

slides.headline: One level can do a lot.
slides.line: A horizontal level marking a repeated reaction area is one of the cleanest beginner tools.

steps.text: Price keeps reacting here. One line marks it.

slides.kicker: Your workspace, not a decoration contest
slides.headline: Clean chart ≠ busy chart.

check.prompt: She adds ten drawing tools, hoping for a clearer read. What happens?

options.label: A better read, more tools always help
options.feedback: More markings isn’t automatically more useful information.

options.label: Price gets harder to read, not easier
options.why: Right. Clutter competes with price for your attention. You don’t need every feature to read a chart well.

slides.headline: Timeframes change your view.
slides.line: Not what’s actually happening in the market underneath.

visual.caption: Same market. Zoomed in or out.

check.prompt: Switching timeframes changes your ___ on the same market.

options.label: Instrument
options.feedback: The instrument doesn’t change just because you zoomed in or out.

options.label: Perspective
options.why: Zooming in or out just changes what detail you can see, not the underlying price story.

options.label: Broker
options.feedback: Your broker has nothing to do with which timeframe you’re viewing.

slides.line: A few tools used clearly is better than a messy chart.

slides.prompt: A member asks why her chart looks so messy. What do you tell her?
slides.modelAnswer: More drawing tools doesn’t mean more clarity, usually it means more clutter. A clean chart uses a few tools clearly, like a couple of horizontal levels marking areas price has reacted to before, so your eyes can find the story instead of fighting through noise.

takeaways: TradingView is a workspace for reading price, not a decoration contest.
A cluttered chart makes price harder to read, not easier.
Switching timeframes changes your view, not the market itself.
remember: A few tools used clearly beats a messy chart.
